The tools that run right after the sliders.
The floors that clip slider results.

faq.q: Why does B COAT plus make it duller?
faq.a: Because blue is backwards. The number is added to the coat value, where bigger means less coat.

faq.q: Why did my slider stop working?
faq.a: The channel reached its floor or ceiling.

faq.q: Can sliders recolour?
faq.a: No. They only change metal, roughness and coat.

faq.q: Slider or SPEC STRENGTH?
faq.a: Use the slider to move one channel. Use strength to scale the whole finish.

mistakes.symptom: Large shifts make the finish look generic.
mistakes.cause: A shift near 100 overwhelms the base values.
mistakes.fix: Choose a different base finish and nudge by 20 to 40.

mistakes.symptom: Wetter did not work on a gel coat.
mistakes.cause: It is already at the floor of 15 and 16.
mistakes.fix: Nothing more to gain. Change the pattern or the paint.

protips: The B COAT slider tooltip in the app says higher is a stronger mirror. The number is really added to the coat value where bigger means duller, so judge by eye.
Save a good slider set as a Feel so it can be reused on other zones.

articles.title: Material override, remap and lighting mask
articles.summary: Remap changes M/R/CC ranges; sampled Material Override replaces M/R/CC/A; Lighting Mask separately replaces alpha. Their Apply and Clear operations have different scope.
articles.what: Remap rescales spatial material channels but byte quantization can lose fine shade differences. Material Override flattens all four channels including alpha. The inspected common engine order is remap, override, then lighting mask; Flake Studio can contribute afterward. None of these alone proves final native car appearance.
when: You like the shine of one part of a spec and want it elsewhere
You need a quick overall change to an imported spec
Decals look glassy and need to go flat
how: Select the intended Zone and establish the drawn footprint required by the tools.
Inspect existing remap, sampled override and lighting-mask fields before Apply.
Applying remap clears sampled override; Restore Original only clears remap and retains its original override.
Sampler Apply includes alpha and clears the separate lighting mask; clearing a sample does not restore that former mask.
Compare actual composed/exported channels and artwork after editing.

controls.label: Remap Low and High
controls.effect: Squeezes a channel into a new range.

tips: See practical remap and sampled-material guides for transaction and alpha scope.
pitfalls: Remapping can push the coat into the forbidden 1 to 15 band; the app raises it back to 16.

combos.why: Sliders run just before these tools, so a remap or override can overrule a slider.
Lighting Mask is the tool that changes alpha.
The floors run after all three tools.

faq.q: Does material override change alpha?
faq.a: The current sampled override replaces M/R/CC/A, including lighting alpha. The separate Lighting Mask runs afterward when set.

faq.q: Does Restore Original undo all material edits?
faq.a: It removes remap only and retains the original sampled override; it does not restore Base, sliders or the entire project.

protips: Preserve fine detail with adequate range span; a flat sample copies values, not texture.
Numeric presets are starting controls, not native appearance endorsements.

articles.title: Spec blend modes
articles.summary: SPEC BLEND changes encoded material fields through different arithmetic rules. Mode names do not guarantee mirror appearance, angle-dependent hue changes, emission or physical embossing.
articles.what: Named modes act on material arrays and a spatial field. Ghost Carve and Frost Etch can impose a roughness floor inside their helper; Chrome Inlay and Ember Gate use offset activation ramps; Angle Flip has no camera or time input; Depth Press derives directional material edges rather than geometry. Classic modes normalize contributions differently, and Screen has a non-neutral zero-contribution case.
when: A material changes unexpectedly even with a flat or weak field
A named mode is being treated as a guaranteed physical appearance
how: Confirm the active mode and whether the composition branch invokes it.
Check normalization, opacity and coverage separately.
Use the mode diagnostic guide to understand its material changes.
Compare the composed material and protected paint before accepting the result.

controls.label: SPEC BLEND
controls.range: Normal, Ghost Carve, Chrome Inlay, Frost Etch, Angle Flip, Ember Gate, Depth Press, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Hard Light, Soft Light
controls.effect: Chooses how the overlay mixes with the base spec.

tips: Compare modes on the same field and target.
pitfalls: Zero field, zero opacity and a skipped effect are different states.
A normalized field value is not painted-area percentage or physical material fraction.
A mode label does not establish automatic hue animation, emission or changed geometry.

deep.heading: Mode diagnostics
deep.body: The linked diagnostic guides document thresholds, intermediate material values and zero-input cases from actual helper observations. Final composition, clipping, preservation rules and coverage still apply; synthetic calculations do not establish native car appearance.

deep.heading: Different composition paths
deep.body: Named physical modes are available in the active Zone dropdown, but their invocation depends on the selected composition path. Do not assume every spec overlay uses the same helper or that selecting a zero-strength control calls it.

mistakes.symptom: The effect is too strong and everything is chrome.
mistakes.cause: Strength and pattern spec amount both high with Chrome Inlay.
mistakes.fix: Lower strength before the next layer.

mistakes.symptom: Ghost Carve shows nothing.
mistakes.cause: The base colour is too bright, so diffuse colour hides the flashes.
mistakes.fix: Crush the colour near black and judge on a daytime track.

mistakes.symptom: A classic blend washed out my finish.
mistakes.cause: Legacy modes mix values directly.
mistakes.fix: Switch to a named mode or lower strength.

protips: Compare Normal and the named mode side by side before you commit.
Angle Flip is the one to try for a finish that changes between camera angles in replays.

articles.title: Spec patterns and overlay stacks
articles.summary: Spec overlays add material texture through selected M/R/C channels, up to five per base. R-only changes roughness directly without repainting pixels. Coverage multiplies strength; multiple unmuted Solo layers can remain active, while muted Solo layers are excluded.
articles.what: SPEC OVERLAYS holds up to five layers for each base tier: primary and second through fifth bases have separate stacks. Adding or duplicating a sixth layer in the same stack is blocked. Spec overlays change material channels, not paint pixels; changed reflections can still alter the visible impression of colour. Modern surface overlays blend selected M, R and C channels toward material targets through authored coverage and strength. A saved legacy collection can behave differently. In mixed stacks, legacy layers apply before modern surface layers. Each layer offers tuning and comparison controls; use the actual picker collections rather than relying on an old fixed catalog count.
when: You want carbon, brushed or sparkle texture without touching the colour
You want a unique surface on one part of the car
how: Open the zone and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click Add Spec Overlay and pick a pattern.
Choose a modest strength, inspect the selected M, R and C channels, and compare the composed spec. Strength50 is a trial setting, not a promise of subtle texture.
Use Mute and Solo to compare layers.

Use Mute and Solo to identify which layers contribute; turn other Solo flags off when you want to isolate exactly one.

Spec overlays change shine only. If you want visible shapes on the paint, use a pattern.

deep.heading: Coverage and strength work together
deep.body: For modern material-target overlays, the selected channel becomes current+(target-current)*coverage*strength. Zero strength, zero coverage or no selected channels leaves that material operation unchanged. At50percent strength and50percent coverage, only25percent of the target difference is applied. This is the material operation; later composition, channel adjustments and output floors can still change exported values.

deep.heading: Order, legacy layers and Solo
deep.body: Modern layers run sequentially within their stack, so later targets mix with the current result of earlier layers. Saved legacy layers are processed before modern surface layers in a mixed stack; moving a layer stays within its legacy or modern lane. Mute removes a layer from the active set. If any unmuted layer is Solo, all unmuted Solo layers in that stack stay active and the other layers are omitted.

deep.heading: Material texture is not paint texture
deep.body: Spec overlays do not repaint your artwork. R-only changes roughness directly, M-only metallic response, and C-only clearcoat response. None guarantees a particular in-sim appearance: lighting and the rest of the material still matter. Paint-source preservation and sponsor-material protection are separate choices.

examples.goal: Try roughness texture on existing paint.
examples.result: The overlay edits roughness directly through its coverage. It preserves paint pixels but changes how reflections spread; compare at car scale and protect logo material separately.

Where to find each kind of overlay.
Paint patterns and spec overlays both stack to five, but only patterns change colour.

faq.q: How many overlays can I stack?
faq.a: Up to five spec overlays per base tier, not five total per zone. The primary base and second through fifth base tiers each have their own stack; adding or duplicating a sixth in the same stack is blocked.

faq.q: Why does my overlay do nothing in the preview?
faq.a: Overlays change shine only. Check the spec views.

faq.q: What strength should I use?
faq.a: Try a modest strength and inspect the result;50 can be a comparison starting point. A given number does not guarantee subtle flake: coverage, the target material, selected channels and existing stack all matter. Modern surface layers use linear strength, while saved legacy layers can behave differently.

faq.q: Can I mute a layer?
faq.a: Yes. Mute, Solo and Duplicate are on each layer.

faq.q: What does a spec pattern do, like a carbon fibre spec?
faq.a: A spec pattern puts a texture into the shine channels (metal, roughness, clearcoat), so the paint colour stays the same but light bounces differently, for example a carbon weave you only see as it catches light. A paint pattern shows colour. Stack up to five spec overlays per base and use the spec views to see them.

faq.q: Why can I not add a sixth spec overlay?
faq.a: The active picker limits each base stack to five spec overlays, including duplicates. Edit, mute or remove an existing layer, or inspect the separate stack of another base tier; a fifth layer in one stack does not mean every stack is full.

faq.q: Why does Solo show more than one spec overlay?
faq.a: Multiple unmuted Solo layers remain active together within that stack. Turn the other Solo flags off to isolate one. A muted Solo layer does not count as an active Solo layer.

faq.q: Does an R-only spec overlay change my paint colour or metal?
faq.a: The material overlay operation changes only selected roughness when R is the only enabled channel. Paint pixels and the unselected M/C channels are unchanged by that operation. Reflections still change, and later composition can affect the final output.

faq.q: Is fifty percent strength and fifty percent coverage half the effect?
faq.a: For a modern material-target overlay, coverage and strength multiply. 50 percent of each applies25percent of the difference between the current material channel and the overlay target, not half.

faq.q: Will changing the order of spec overlays change the result?
faq.a: It can. Modern overlays mix sequentially, so the later layer works on the material left by the earlier layer. Mixed saved stacks process legacy layers before modern layers, and moves stay within the legacy or modern lane.

faq.q: Does a spec overlay repaint my sponsor logo?
faq.a: It does not repaint logo pixels, but it can change the material response over the logo where its coverage and zone mask apply. Protect sponsor material separately using suitable zone targeting and restrictions; keeping paint colours is not automatic material protection.

faq.q: Why is my spec overlay invisible at full strength?
faq.a: Check Mute/Solo, selected channels, coverage, zone targeting and whether the target differs from the current material. Full strength cannot affect pixels with zero coverage. Check spec views rather than expecting a visible paint pattern.

faq.q: Does zero spec overlay strength change anything?
faq.a: In the modern material overlay operation, zero strength is an exact no-op. Zero coverage and an empty channel selection are also no-ops. Other layers, base material and later adjustments may still be visible.

mistakes.symptom: Everything looks noisy.
mistakes.cause: Several overlays at high strength on all three channels.
mistakes.fix: Solo each layer, tick fewer channels, lower strength.

mistakes.symptom: The old stack disappeared.
mistakes.cause: Setting overlays through an apply command replaces the stack.
mistakes.fix: Add layers one at a time with Add Spec Overlay.

protips: A subtle flake overlay at strength 30 to 50 adds depth to almost any finish.
Pick the channel on purpose. The same pattern on R, on M and on C gives three different looks.

articles.title: Spec presets and Feels
articles.summary: A Feel replaces three material shift fields, not a complete finish. User presets are local, built-in names take precedence, and a Saved toast does not prove storage persistence. Preserve the full project separately.
articles.what: saveSpecPreset records only r, g and b shift fields. Base identity, stack, texture scale, masks and source-layer targets are not saved in this preset. Keep a project or layered source for an editable setup; a named Feel alone cannot reconstruct it. applySpecPreset assigns the clamped triplet to specShiftR/G/B, replacing the existing fields. Reapplying the same Feel sets the same numbers rather than accumulating a second dose. Auto-Pop is a different additive operation. The apply handler looks up the built-in name before user storage. A user preset with an identical built-in name can be saved, but the built-in triplet wins when applying that name. Give custom Feels distinct names and inspect the resulting sliders. The save handler directly assigns store[name] after trimming the submitted name. It does not ask for an overwrite confirmation. Use a distinct name if the previous triplet must remain available. This handler stores Feels in browser localStorage under spbSpecPresets. Storage belongs to that app/browser origin; it is not account synchronization or an exported finish library. A different port, browser profile or cleared app storage can expose a different list. The storage-write helper catches localStorage errors without surfacing them, and the save handler still updates the in-memory store and shows success. A blocked or full store can therefore leave a session-only preset. Verify persistence after reopening before relying on it. _loadSpecPresets returns the cached window._spbSpecPresets when present. It does not reread localStorage every time. Another window or external storage edit is not guaranteed to update this editor’s cached list until its state is refreshed. The save handler rereads zones[index] after the dialog. It captures the then-current shifts at that index, not a stable object snapshot taken before the dialog. If Zones were reordered, verify which Zone supplied the triplet before trusting the new preset. The save handler trims outer whitespace and skips an empty or cancelled name. It uses the resulting string as the exact storage key; it does not normalize case. Names differing only by case can be separate presets and can be easy to confuse. The apply handler parses each value as an integer, falls back to zero for invalid parsed values and clamps to minus127 through plus127. Decimal text is truncated by parseInt, not a floating-point material setting. Check the applied triplet when importing or editing storage data. deleteSpecPreset removes an entry from the user store. Built-in Feels remain in their constant table, and name lookup still prefers them. Deleting the user shadow does not delete the shipped Wet Candy or other built-in entry. The delete handler removes the stored named entry and refreshes the UI. It does not restore Zone shift values or create a Zone Undo transaction for a previously applied Feel. Change or undo the Zone adjustment separately if that is the intention. The reviewed engine applies channel shifts before material remap, material override, lighting-mask handling and optional Flake processing. Those later enabled operations can change the final map. A slider triplet is not a complete description of final exported pixels. The reviewed engine shift is multiplied by clipped Zone mask coverage before each channel is clamped. Partial coverage can apply less of a shift, and later gates or material controls still matter. Inspect boundaries rather than interpreting the preset numbers as uniform final bytes. The client Feel handler sets only R/G/B shift fields. The reviewed shift loop modifies only those three material channels; lighting-mask handling is a separate later operation. Do not treat a Feel as an alpha repair or a guarantee that other enabled controls leave alpha unchanged.

For a custom Feel, use a distinct name and verify persistence after reopening. Keep the complete project separately.

faq.q: Why does Auto-Pop say the spec analyzer is not ready?
faq.a: The handler requires SPB_SpecStats.computeZoneSpecStats. If unavailable it returns before changing shifts. Reloading can restore the module, but does not prove the loaded preview matches the current paint; check that separately before trying again.

faq.q: Can Auto-Pop work from the paint image when no spec preview has loaded?
faq.a: The handler reads livePreviewSpecImg and requires its source and natural width. The paint image alone is not its input. A missing loaded spec preview causes an early return rather than a blind material recommendation.

faq.q: Does Auto-Pop check that its spec preview came from the latest Zone settings?
faq.a: The inspected handler checks that a readable spec image exists, but does not compare a job ID or render hash with the current Zone state. Wait for the intended preview to finish and inspect it before measuring. Old preview data can produce a suggestion for earlier settings.

faq.q: Does Auto-Pop always restrict analysis to my drawn Zone region?
faq.a: It passes regionMask only when its length equals paint-canvas width times height. A mismatched mask supplies no mask options to the analyzer. The resulting suggestion should not be described as a validated measurement of that drawn region.

faq.q: Does Auto-Pop resolve my sponsor layer and colour picks into the analyzer mask?
faq.a: The inspected handler supplies only a correctly sized regionMask and dimensions to the analyzer. It does not build sourceLayer/sourceLayers or colour-selection coverage there. The preview contains composed material, but this call does not prove an exact sponsor-only statistical target.

faq.q: Why can Auto-Pop suggest shifts even when the analyzer label describes mixed materials?
faq.a: Auto-Pop reads the three mean fields. The analyzer can label a channel using median or mixed-population information. A mean-based nudge does not replace inspection of separate chrome and matte areas; a mixed-material Zone may need more specific targeting.

faq.q: Does “nothing to pop” prove every selected pixel has ideal gloss?
faq.a: Small proposed changes round to multiples of five and can become zero. The handler then returns without a shift. That message is not per-pixel visual approval, a calibrated gloss measurement or evidence that every material in a mixed Zone is already ideal.

faq.q: Should I click Auto-Pop several times before the new preview finishes?
faq.a: Each nonzero Auto-Pop adds deltas to the existing shifts. Clicking again while the same preview is still displayed can reuse its old means and add another change before seeing the result. Wait and compare rather than treating repeated clicks as new measurements.

faq.q: Can Auto-Pop report a boost when my shift slider is already at its limit?
faq.a: It computes proposed deltas first, then clamps the accumulated fields to minus127 through plus127. A saturated field may remain unchanged even though the toast names a nonzero proposed delta. Check the actual slider and output, not only the boost message.

faq.q: What happens if Auto-Pop cannot read or analyze the spec pixels?
faq.a: Read errors, analysis exceptions or a null analysis result return before the shift assignment and Undo push. The handler reports a problem rather than creating a new material. Preserve the source and inspect the preview/target instead of resetting artwork to fix this message.

articles.title: The Spec Map Inspector
articles.summary: Read raw stored material values from the loaded spec preview, using Point or per-channel median sampling. Whole-map statistics and tinted views have different purposes and do not prove the latest edits are rendered.
articles.what: Open Material Sampler from Spec Tools, or Channels beside the rendered view. Some layouts place Material Sampler under Mask > Advanced spec utilities. ALL, R, G, B and A change only the display. Point reads one raw pixel; 3x3 and 5x5 Median combine per-channel neighborhood medians. Min, max and mean cover the whole loaded map. You want to copy a material from one place to another

deep.heading: Seeing the real numbers

deep.heading: Finding and copying a material
deep.body: Select Connected grows from the clicked pixel across touching similar pixels; Select All Similar finds every matching pixel on the car. Material tolerance runs from 0 to 64 with a default of 12. Copy M, R, CC and A copy the numbers, and Apply to Active Zone writes them as an override for the zone. Clear Zone Override removes the sampled override; it does not restore the prior override or lighting mask like an Undo snapshot.

deep.heading: The material readout
deep.body: After a preview renders, the app also reports the material mix of the whole spec as a bar: percent glossy, metallic and matte, with plain warnings for flat or whitewashed settings, such as coat in the 1 to 15 dead band or a metal floor too low. Treat it as a quick check before you export.

articles.title: Colour shift and angle reveal
articles.summary: Separate colour-bearing texture, encoded material channels, COLOR FLIP treatment and observed car lighting. Reviewed Ghost/Chameleon/Nightshift functions do not take camera angle or time; no universal dark-base or guaranteed reflection-colour recipe is established. The Angle Flip spec-blend helper likewise uses a spatial field with no camera/time input; native hue inversion is not guaranteed.
articles.what: The reviewed finish functions generate RGB paint and M/R/Cc texture arrays. Some preserve input RGB in their own paint function, while others generate or blend a palette. Neither a family name nor a spec-driven intent proves source-colour preservation or automatic hue travel. The inspected Color Lab applies YIQ hue rotation to the dark-value population of RGB using a degree setting; it does not use camera angle. These source facts do not prove the lit car looks identical across views, and do not guarantee a particular teal/gold flash, a day/night switch, or universal dark-base/scale thresholds. Earlier Ghost Shift or crushed-palette recipes are comparison ideas, not accepted per-car recommendations. Physical panel or UV placement is not established by texture coordinates.

A shift finish looks flat head on

deep.heading: Evidence scope
deep.body: Reviewed Ghost factory and separate Ghost Panel functions, three active Chameleon references, Nightshift Cyanide Hour and Color Lab math establish array-generation behavior. No renderer, car shader or native painting was invoked in this audit. Fine-feature owner doctrine guides design; it is not proof that every pattern above one size loses its effect.

faq.q: Is dark paint required for every angle-reveal finish?
faq.a: No universal requirement is established. A darker palette can be a comparison option, but the exact paint construction, material channels, contribution and lighting matter. Do not replace a finish’s own palette or crush protected artwork solely because a family is called shift.

faq.q: Will clearcoat automatically flash teal and gold on every car?
faq.a: Those exact colours are not guaranteed by a clearcoat texture or finish name. The inspected functions produce paint and material arrays, not a per-car camera/light result. Compare the actual composed car; do not infer specific reflection colours from a combined spec preview.

faq.q: Does hot pink in the combined spec preview mean pink paint will flip colour?
faq.a: No. Combined spec RGB encodes metallic, roughness and clearcoat channels rather than decorative paint colours. Inspect the paint image separately. A pink-looking spec tuple is not evidence of pink paint or an angle-dependent colour flip.

faq.q: Does the flat paint preview prove how a finish looks at night?
faq.a: No. A paint-only image shows RGB texture without establishing the actual car’s lighting and material response. Inspect M/R/Cc and the composed result, then compare the car under the intended conditions. This review does not establish a universal night visibility rule.

faq.q: Can COLOR FLIP use camera angle instead of changing the saved paint RGB?
faq.a: The inspected Color Lab applies a dark-value-weighted YIQ hue rotation to RGB arrays using a degree setting. It has no live camera-angle input. That operation changes texture colour treatment; camera motion and lighting are separate from its source math.

articles.summary: Ghost Carve interpolates coat toward64–240 by field and opacity. A zero field is not off; its invoked helper also floors roughness at16 even at zero opacity.
articles.what: No. At full strength, a zero field targets clearcoat64 rather than leaving it alone. An incoming coat200 becomes64 in the helper. A flat field can therefore change material without creating a visible texture; final appearance still depends on composition and lighting. A field of0.5 targets coat152 at full strength:64+176×0.5. That is an encoded channel value, not50% gloss. With input M/R/CC100/100/16 the helper gives100/87.5/152 before final output processing. Not inside this helper: it still clips roughness to at least16. A roughness2 input becomes16 even with zero blend opacity. This describes the helper when invoked, not a promise that a disabled UI option will invoke it. Compare actual composed output when preserving a low-roughness material. It interpolates the encoded coat value toward the field target. With incoming coat200 and a zero field, half opacity gives132 rather than a physical half-gloss response. Keep the distinction between arithmetic channel blending and the visible material.

how: Identify the active material blend mode and the source field.
Separate field normalization, blend opacity and final coverage.
